ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, it is known that the coordinates of point $C$ are $(\sqrt{3}, -2)$, and the line $AB$ intersects the $x$ axis and $y$ axis at point $A$ and point $B$ respectively, with the coordinates of point $B$ being $(0, 3)$, and $\angle BAO = 30^\circ$. What is the analytical equation of line $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Since $B(0, 3)$, it follows that $OB=3$. In the right triangle $\triangle AOB$, we have $\angle AOB=90^\circ$ and $\angle BAO=30^\circ$. Therefore, $AB=2OB=6$ and $OA=\sqrt{AB^{2}-OB^{2}}=3\sqrt{3}$. Hence, $A(3\sqrt{3}, 0)$. Let the equation of line $AB$ be $y=kx+b$. Substituting points $A(3\sqrt{3}, 0)$ and $B(0, 3)$ gives $\begin{cases}3\sqrt{3}k+b=0\\ b=3\end{cases}$. Solving, we find $\begin{cases}k=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\\ b=3\end{cases}$. Thus, the equation of line $AB$ is $y=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x+3$; hence, the answer is $\boxed{y=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x+3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, the x-axis points to the right, and the y-axis points upward. The line AB intersects the y-axis at the upper point B, and intersects the x-axis at the right-side point A. The line segment AB slopes from B down to the right to A. The point C is also marked in the figure near the fourth quadrant, but it is not on the line AB and has no effect on finding the equation of AB. The problem gives the coordinates of B as (0,3), and angle BAO as 30°. Reasoning: Because A is on the positive half-axis of the x-axis, the ray AO from A to O is along the negative x direction. Also because ∠BAO=30°, the direction from A to B is 30° above the negative x-axis direction, that is, the direction angle relative to the positive x-axis is 180°-30°=150°. Therefore the slope of the line AB is k=tan150°=-√3/3. Also B=(0,3) is the intersection point of the line AB and the y-axis, so the y-intercept b=3. Substituting into the line form y=kx+b, the equation of the line AB is obtained as y=-(√3/3)x+3.
